drivingQuestion: Prayer has set times, so why are women obligated in it, and why did the mishna need to state it?
outcomeNote: Prayer is obligatory for women because it is a plea for mercy; the verse fixing three times does not make it time-bound.

segments.he: וְחַיָּיבִין בִּתְפִלָּה. דְּרַחֲמֵי נִינְהוּ. מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב בַּהּ ״עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר וְצָהֳרַיִם״, כְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא דָּמֵי — קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: We also learned in the mishna that women, slaves, and children are «obligated in prayer.» The Gemara explains that, although the mitzva of prayer is only in effect at particular times, which would lead to the conclusion that women are exempt, nevertheless, since prayer «is» supplication for «mercy» and women also require divine mercy, they are obligated. However, «lest you say: Since» regarding prayer it is «written: “Evening and morning and afternoon» I pray and cry aloud and He hears my voice” (Psalms 55:18), perhaps prayer should be «considered a time-bound, positive mitzva» and women would be exempt, the mishna «teaches us» that, fundamentally, the mitzva of prayer is not time-bound and, therefore, everyone is obligated.
